title: Robotics: Algorithms and Control
description: Kinematic and dynamic modeling of robots; configuration space; motion planning algorithms; control of robots; sensors and perception; reasoning; mobile robots.

title: Mechatronic Embedded Systems Design
description: Design and fabrication of scaled-down autonomous vehicles from an embedded-systems perspective: motors, microcontrollers, power supply, sensors and control algorithms, culminating in a racing competition.

title: Control Engineering
description: Continuous- and discrete-time state-space models; solutions to state equations; stability; reachability/controllability; state feedback and tracking; observability, observers, output feedback; optimal control and estimation.

title: Principles of Automatic Control
description: Transfer functions; block diagrams; flow graphs; state-space canonical forms; stability analysis; digital control methods.

title: Linear Systems Theory and Design
description: State-variable description, linear operators, impulse-response matrix, controllability, observability, and state-feedback design.

title: Optimal Control
description: Optimal control of dynamic systems in continuous and discrete time; maximum principle; dynamic programming and constraints.

title: Nonlinear Control
description: Nonlinear phenomena, linear and piecewise-linear approximations, describing functions, servomechanisms, phase plane, limit cycles, and Lyapunov stability theory.

title: Introduction to Embedded Systems
description: Microcontrollers, instruction sets, data representation, assembly and mixed C/assembly programming, memory organization, interrupt processing, and I/O interfacing.

title: Image Analysis and Computer Vision I
description: Image formation, geometry and stereo; 2-D image analysis by Fourier and other transforms; image enhancement, color, and segmentation.

title: Image Analysis and Computer Vision II
description: 2-D and 3-D shape representation, segmentation, camera and stereo modeling, motion, and generic object and face recognition.

title: Pattern Recognition I
description: Design of automated systems for detection, recognition, classification and diagnosis using parametric and nonparametric decision-making techniques.

title: Detection and Estimation Theory
description: Bayes, Neyman-Pearson and minimax detection for discrete- and continuous-time random processes; estimation of random and non-random signal parameters.

title: Adaptive Digital Filters
description: Optimal filters, Wiener and Kalman filters; signal modeling; adaptive filters for channel equalization, echo and noise cancellation, and linear prediction.

title: Neural Networks
description: Neuron models, learning methods, the perceptron, nonlinear optimization, backpropagation, associative memory, Hopfield networks, SVM, SOM, PCA, convolutional networks and deep learning.

title: Social Robotics and Human-Robot Interaction
description: Research and design in human-robot interaction: user mental models, social cues, interaction modeling, anthropomorphism, verbal and non-verbal communication and emotion, environmental mapping, proxemics, and AI/ML/NLP in robotics.

title: Special Topics: Probabilistic Robotics
description: Recursive state estimation, Markov localization, Monte Carlo localization, and simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM). Offered periodically as a special-topics section.

title: Artificial Intelligence I
description: Intelligence and AI, autonomous agents, agent architectures and environment types, search and adversarial search, search in complex environments, logic and probability, learning, and generative AI.

title: Artificial Intelligence II
description: Predicate logic and resolution, reasoning under uncertainty and incomplete information, state and change, planning, temporal reasoning, knowledge representation, learning, and advanced search.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
description: Mechanism, implementation and application of systems that improve from experience: classification, density estimation, clustering, and online learning.

title: Advanced Machine Learning
description: Structured data modeling, probabilistic inference for big data, deep learning, and large-scale optimization.

title: Computer Vision I
description: Image filtering, feature detection, description and matching, image segmentation, and object recognition, with hands-on projects.

title: Advanced Computer Vision
description: Analysis of 3-D scene images: shape from shading, texture and line drawings, surface orientation and representation, and reconstruction of 3-D scenes.

title: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
description: Convolutional networks for object recognition, recurrent networks for video modeling, generative adversarial networks, and attention models.

title: Automation and Robotics Applications
description: Robot kinematics and dynamics; robot design; trajectory planning; and pneumatic and hydraulic system design with practical applications.

title: Mechatronics I
description: Elements of mechatronic systems: sensors, actuators, microcontrollers, modeling and hardware-in-the-loop simulation, with an electromechanical laboratory.

title: Robotic Manipulators
description: Description of robotic manipulators; gripper trajectory execution; manipulator design, degrees of freedom, mobility and workspace; special link positions; static and dynamic force transmission.

title: Mechatronics II
description: Microcontrollers in electro-mechanical systems for measurement and control; interface hardware; real-time software and development tools; applications in robotic motion control and factory automation.

title: Wearable Robots for Assistance and Rehabilitation
description: Wearable robots that help people with disabilities and control methods for electromechanical devices that physically interact with humans, such as robotic prostheses and exoskeletons.

title: Virtual Automation
description: Manufacturing and automation modeling with CAD/CAM and computer-integrated manufacturing; virtual manufacturing; industrial robots and automated factory models within virtual environments.

title: Automatic Control of Mechanical Systems
description: System modeling and performance evaluation; modern control-system design and analysis; real-time computer control of engines, manufacturing processes and biomechanical systems.

title: Dynamic Systems Analysis I
description: Classical control theory, feedback, Laplace transforms and transfer functions, and compensator design.

title: Dynamic Systems and Control
description: Dynamics of linear systems and the analysis and design of feedback control systems for mechanical systems, using analytical and computational approaches.

title: Mechanisms and Dynamics of Machinery
description: Kinematic analysis and synthesis of mechanisms: linkages, cams, spur gears and gear trains; dynamic forces in machines, applicable to manipulator design.

title: Advanced Kinematics I
description: Kinematic synthesis of planar linkages with higher-order, precision-point and approximate synthesis, and a unified treatment of position, function and path-angle problems.

title: Advanced Kinematics II
description: Spatial transformations and displacements; design for body guidance; closure analysis, branching, rotatability, differential kinematics and numerical solutions.

title: Dynamics of Mechanical Systems
description: Advanced dynamical analysis: Lagrange's equation, Hamilton's principle, and Newton-Euler equations for rigid bodies, fundamental to robot dynamics.

title: Engineering Dynamics
description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies, with kinematics in several coordinate systems and kinetics including Newton's second law and impact analysis. Foundation for robotics coursework.

title: Neural Engineering I: Introduction to Hybrid Neural Systems
description: Modeling and design of functional neural interfaces for in vivo and in vitro applications; electrodes and molecular coatings; neural prostheses and biopotential control of robotics.

title: Human Augmentics
description: Technologies for augmentation of human capabilities: human limitations, implants and wearable technologies, brain-computer interfaces, exoskeletons, and sensors and networks, with project work.

title: Human Movement and Neural Control
description: Musculoskeletal biomechanics and neural control of human movement: measurement (EEG, fMRI, EMG, force sensors, motion tracking), rigid-body dynamics, modeling, control theory and motor learning.

title: Sensory Prostheses Engineering
description: Prosthetic devices for damaged sensory systems: physiology, technology and information flow in hybrid systems, including visual, auditory, neuromuscular and haptic applications.

title: Biocontrol
description: Characteristics of physiological systems using the framework of linear systems and control theory; stability and its relationship to pathology and control function.

title: Neural Engineering I Laboratory
description: Hands-on experience with engineered neural systems, emphasizing neuroprostheses and biosensors through computational and experimental models.
